items.stem: A team reports an AI feature's cost as only the per-1K-token API price. What is the main flaw in this view?

options.text: It ignores compute, retrieval, storage and operational costs
options.rationale: Correct: total cost of an AI feature spans more than token pricing.

options.text: Token price is irrelevant to AI cost
options.rationale: Token price is a real driver, just not the only one.
Latency is a separate axis; cost still matters.

options.text: API pricing never changes so cost is fixed
options.rationale: Pricing and usage both vary; cost is not fixed.

items.explanation: Correct: token price is one driver; total cost includes compute, retrieval, storage and operations.

items.stem: Which TWO techniques can reduce user-perceived latency without changing the model? (Select TWO.)

options.rationale: Correct: cache hits avoid inference entirely.

options.text: Streaming tokens as they are generated
options.rationale: Correct: streaming reduces time-to-first-token perceived by users.

options.text: Adding more retrieval sources per request

items.explanation: Correct: caching repeated results and streaming tokens both cut perceived wait.

items.stem: An AI feature costs 0.20 per use and saves 2.00 of staff time per use. What does this tell you about ROI?

options.text: Net value per use is positive, so the unit economics are favourable
options.rationale: Correct: 2.00 saved exceeds 0.20 cost per use.

options.text: ROI is negative because the feature has any cost
options.rationale: Cost alone does not make ROI negative; it is offset by savings.

options.text: ROI cannot be estimated without the model's accuracy
options.rationale: Accuracy affects realised savings but a first-pass ROI is still estimable.

options.text: The feature must be free to have positive ROI
options.rationale: ROI depends on net value, not zero cost.

items.explanation: Correct: net value per use is positive (2.00 saved minus 0.20 cost), supporting a favourable ROI before scaling effects.
